name: genvid-skills
description: Genvid reference skill pack: teaches any agent that loads Agent Skills to drive the Genvid governed boundary.
migration_notes: 0.1.0 -> 0.2.0 (breaking): composition inference moved to the BYOK agent (#1667). The composition skills author structure themselves and cite verbatim screenplay quotes as content anchors instead of running the billable breakdown_* tools. storyboard_write compose payload is now Scene -> Beat -> Shot (a beats[] level was added between scene and shots), every shot carries provenance:{quote, scene?}, and scenes_write linked_assets items carry an optional provenance anchor; raw block_ids are rejected. breakdown_assets / breakdown_storyboard are no longer used by the pack's composition skills. boundary_compat narrowed from '>=0.1.0 <0.2.0' to '>=0.2.0 <0.3.0' (#1966) to match the pack version bump above, per the policy in README.md#compatibility. The range is now verified against the live boundary: scripts/boundary_client.py (#1992) reads the boundary contract version off the MCP `initialize` handshake (serverInfo.version, currently '0.2.0', deliberately bumped when the tool contract changes) and Gate 2 checks it against this range instead of skipping. 0.2.0 -> 0.2.1 (additive): new genvid-media-registration skill for the registered offline residency tier (#2025), driving the additive register_media boundary tool that landed in #2022. register_media is additive to the boundary contract (a new sibling of ingest_generated_media, no breaking change), so serverInfo.version stays '0.2.0' and boundary_compat is unchanged — this is a patch bump, not a minor. 0.2.1 -> 0.3.0 (breaking): the retired composition tools breakdown_assets, breakdown_storyboard, and sync_assets_with_screenplay were removed from the boundary (#1171) — Genvid funds composition inference on no surface. serverInfo.version bumps 0.2.0 -> 0.3.0 and boundary_compat narrows to '>=0.3.0 <0.4.0'. The pack's composition skills already author structure via the governed write tools (scenes_write / assets_write / shots_write / storyboard_write) and did not call the removed tools; the two skills that named them as billable examples (genvid-generator-connections, genvid-orientation) are reworded to the write-tool framing. 0.3.0 -> 0.4.0 (breaking): storyboard_write method='compose' now STAGES a pending review instead of writing live (#2139) — on a project that already has a production storyboard the composed result lands in *_pending + diff and is invisible to production reads until an Accept promotes it (POST /projects/{id}/storyboard/actions/approve). The compose response gains status ('pending_review' | 'applied') and diff_summary. A first compose onto an empty project still lands directly to production (status 'applied'). This is a breaking observable-behavior change for any agent flow that composed then read production expecting the write to be live, so serverInfo.version bumps 0.3.0 -> 0.4.0 and boundary_compat narrows to '>=0.4.0 <0.5.0'. insert is unchanged (post-certification additive change-order, applied live). Customer-facing SKILL.md wording (compose-goes-live -> compose-stages-review) rides the #2089-S3/#2110 re-sync wave and is applied under separate approval. 0.4.0 -> 0.5.0 (breaking): removed the write-triggered storyboard regen path (#2128) — the screenplay_write tool's regenerate_storyboard input field, which forced a full deterministic Fountain-parse re-derive of the storyboard on every governed screenplay write, is gone. Agent-owned storyboard_write(method="compose") is now the sole producer of a composed storyboard; the governed screenplay write path produces a screenplay only. serverInfo.version bumps 0.4.0 -> 0.5.0 and boundary_compat narrows to '>=0.5.0 <0.6.0'. insert/compose are unaffected. 0.5.0 -> 0.5.1 (additive): the BYOM dialogue bind path shipped (#1743) — ingest_generated_media's link_type now accepts shot_dialog (bind a shot's dialogue/audio, render_type TTS or S2S) at parity with the existing keyframe/video bind paths, closing the #1723 assignment-circumvention gap for audio. genvid-agent-generation's audio row is promoted from forward-looking to a worked example (claim the audio task -> generate with your own TTS/S2S model -> bind shot_dialog), with a one-line note on the two axes (claim/bind on task_type="audio"; price on production_read generation_type="dialog"). This is additive to the boundary tool contract — link_type was already a free string, so only the field's description and server-side acceptance changed, not the param schema — so serverInfo.version stays '0.5.0' and boundary_compat is unchanged: a patch bump, not a minor. 0.5.1 -> 0.5.2 (additive): genvid-orientation and genvid-agent-generation gain an explicit preflight — before the first generation step, confirm a provider is wired into your client, and if none, wire the provider's own MCP server (Genvid never sees the key) — closing the discoverability gap where the boundary's bring-your-own-provider posture was learnable only by exhausting tool search (#2200). This is prose only; no boundary tool contract or param schema changed, so serverInfo.version stays '0.5.0' and boundary_compat is unchanged ('>=0.5.0 <0.6.0'): a patch bump, not a minor. 0.5.2 -> 0.5.3 (additive, republish): republishes content already merged into source under 0.5.2 but never pushed to the public mirror, so the published pack matches source again. genvid-skills-publish.yml is manual (workflow_dispatch), and additive edits that skip a version bump let source silently drift from the published pack under one version string (#2445). Two additive/docs-only changes are affected: the #2200 provider-wiring preflight (#2415) in genvid-agent-generation + genvid-orientation (before the first generation step, confirm a provider is wired; if none, wire the provider's own MCP server — Genvid never sees the key), and the #2350 SFX/music bind sections (#2388) in genvid-agent-generation (generate a shot's sound effects / music with your own model and bind via ingest_generated_media). No boundary tool contract or param schema changed, so serverInfo.version stays '0.5.0' and boundary_compat is unchanged ('>=0.5.0 <0.6.0'): a patch bump, not a minor. The drift itself is now gated: scripts/check_version_bump.py fails any PR that edits published pack content (all of genvid-skills/ except the dev-only scripts/ and tests/) without bumping this version, so publishable content can no longer ship under a stale version. 0.5.3 -> 0.5.4 (additive): the boundary feedback surface (#2423) declares two new tools in the pack references as status 'designed' — review_read (read status-history transitions, review comments, auto-demotion provenance) and review_write (record_decision / record_finding / record_chain_summary decision-event writes). Reference docs only (_boundary_tools.yaml + boundary-tools.md); the tools flip to 'live' in the post-deploy follow-up once the prod boundary serves them. No live boundary tool contract or param schema changed, so serverInfo.version stays '0.5.0' and boundary_compat is unchanged ('>=0.5.0 <0.6.0'): a patch bump, not a minor. 0.5.4 -> 0.5.5 (additive): genvid-agent-generation now teaches the local-file bind path (#2442). A local generator (OpenAI Codex built-in image generation, a local ComfyUI) writes bytes to disk and never returns a hosted URL, so the pack's two documented transports left image_base64 as the only option — silently lossy at full resolution (#1812). Step 2 now routes by what the generator produced: hosted URL -> ingest_generated_media source_url (unchanged); local file -> the genvid CLI's `import-generated-media ... -c multipart 'rendered_output: @<path>'`, which streams the file byte-for-byte to the same route, same attestation, same task-claim gate. image_base64 is demoted to genuinely tiny payloads with an explicit truncation warning. Docs only: no boundary tool contract or param schema changed, so serverInfo.version stays '0.5.0' and boundary_compat is unchanged — a patch bump. The CLI op itself (importGeneratedMedia, admitted to the CLI at Tier 2 by #2442) ships in a genvid CLI release, not in this pack. 0.5.5 -> 0.5.6 (additive): make the genvid CLI local-file bind path discoverable outside genvid-agent-generation Step 2 (#2541, follows #2442). README gains a scoped 'The genvid CLI — required to bind locally-generated files' prerequisite section (install via brew / install.sh + genvid login, called out as needed only for the local-file path, not for hosted-URL-only users), and genvid-agent-generation's first-frame worked example now shows the local-file CLI variant inline (not only in the general Step 2 routing). Companion change outside the pack: the MCP ingest_generated_media tool description now points local-file callers at the client-side CLI, since the remote server can't read local disk and base64 corrupts a full-res file. Docs only: no boundary tool contract or param schema changed, so serverInfo.version stays '0.5.0' and boundary_compat is unchanged ('>=0.5.0 <0.6.0') — a patch bump. 0.5.6 -> 0.5.7 (additive, correction): the reference comment describing ingest_generated_media's attestation semantics said it certifies at the 'verified tier' (_boundary_tools.yaml). #2575 established that this is exactly the over-claim it removed: an ingest carries a generation record the CUSTOMER's agent reports, so Genvid signs externally_attested and certifies at the ATTESTED tier — it holds the bytes but did not witness the generation. The comment now says so. Comment only: no tool contract, param schema, or customer-facing skill prose changed, and boundary-tools.md does not surface the tier, so serverInfo.version stays '0.5.0' and boundary_compat is unchanged ('>=0.5.0 <0.6.0') — a patch bump, not a minor. 0.5.7 -> 0.6.0 (breaking): the published contract is promoted from 20 tools to the 27 the boundary supports, and the genvid-budgeting skill is removed from the pack. Four already-deployed tools were still published 'designed': review_read / review_write (#2423), finalize_media_registration (#2207), and connect_media (#2283) flip 'designed' -> 'live', all verified name-by-name against a live tools/list on 2026-07-27. Tools the contract never listed are added, among them approve_media (the boundary's media selection surface, #2195) and export_provenance_report (the production audit-trail export, #2212), whose absence made the published contract read as though the boundary had neither an approval surface nor a provenance record. The header now states the scope rule outright: this file is the supported surface, and every tool on it is validated against prod by the smoke test. genvid-budgeting is removed because the whole-production budgeting and shoot-schedule betas it drove are not part of that surface (#2281; #2615 tracks the backend work); a pack that ships a skill teaching tools the contract does not publish is the same drift in a different file. Removing a published skill is breaking for anyone who installed 0.5.6, hence the minor bump rather than a patch. Two corrections ride along. production_write was published as 'additive' but registers DESTRUCTIVE in code — its update methods overwrite existing project and task state — so the published classification understated the risk of a live tool. And the blanket claim that every billable/destructive call is audit-logged in entity_events is now scoped to what the audit trigger actually covers — project, sequence, scene, beat, shot, asset, screenplay, media, and signed-manifest writes, plus the links binding media to shots and assets and any change to a media's locator: review_write records a decision_event instead, and a task's workflow_status transitions are recorded in the review history review_read returns. The classification column is a risk signal, not an audit guarantee, and now says so. No boundary tool contract or param schema changed, so serverInfo.version stays '0.5.0' and boundary_compat is unchanged ('>=0.5.0 <0.6.0') — the minor bump is the pack's own surface changing, not the boundary's. 0.6.0 -> 0.6.1 (additive, correction): genvid-agent-generation's video section now states explicitly that binding a shot_video also selects it for the single-cardinality slot, at parity with a first frame — no separate select call is needed before the shot's video task can go to review (#2455). Prose only: no tool contract or param schema changed, so serverInfo.version stays '0.5.0' and boundary_compat is unchanged ('>=0.5.0 <0.6.0') — a patch bump, not a minor. 0.6.1 -> 0.6.2 (docs correction): README's Compatibility section described a state that no longer holds (#2663). The boundary_compat example showed '>=0.2.0 <0.3.0' while pack.json carries '>=0.5.0 <0.6.0', and the caveat still claimed get_boundary_contract() and a boundary_client module did not exist yet and that Gate 2 in scripts/smoke_test.py SKIPs unconditionally. Both shipped: scripts/boundary_client.py reads the contract version off the MCP initialize handshake (serverInfo.version) and Gate 2 checks the declared range against a live boundary whenever BOUNDARY_URL is set, skipping only when none is configured. The section now says what the code does, and the runtime version is named as serverInfo.version rather than the design-era 'boundary_contract_version' field, which was never implemented under that name. Docs only: no boundary tool contract or param schema changed, so serverInfo.version stays '0.5.0' and boundary_compat is unchanged ('>=0.5.0 <0.6.0') - a patch bump, not a minor. 0.6.2 -> 0.6.3 (additive, backport): lands the content that existed only on the public mirror, so source is a strict superset of the published pack again and a publish is purely additive (#2665). The mirror is a publish target, not a place to author, but it is writable and the Article 50 work was committed straight into it: skills/genvid-article50-readiness/ (released there as v0.6.1), its README section, and a copy scrub across README.md. Because genvid-skills-publish.yml rsyncs without --delete, a publish from source would have dropped the skill from this skills array while leaving its directory on the mirror as an orphan, deleted the README section, and reverted the scrub. The skill directory is copied byte-identical from the mirror and registered below, and the mirror's scrubbed README wording is adopted wherever the two differed, keeping this repo's own #2455 shot_video sentence and the #2663 Compatibility correction, which the mirror does not carry yet. The skill itself is the first in the pack that drives NO boundary tool and needs no Genvid account, no MCP connection and no network access: a stdlib-only Python CLI (article50_scan.py, shipped beside SKILL.md rather than under a scripts/ subdirectory, because the publish rsync strips any directory named scripts/ or tests/ at every depth) reads what each file carries in its own bytes - content credentials (JPEG APP11 JUMBF, PNG caBX, WebP C2PA chunk, BMFF uuid box, .c2pa sidecars), the IPTC digital source type in XMP, generator metadata, sidecars - reconciles that against an operator-authored article50.json declaration, and emits a machine-readable disclosure report plus a gap list. Its scope limits are stated in the skill and printed in every report: it reports evidence and the absence of evidence, it does NOT determine compliance and its output is not legal advice; imperceptible watermarks are not assessed; content-credential detection is presence-only and never validates a signature or its trust chain. Additive: no boundary tool contract or param schema changed and no existing skill was edited, so serverInfo.version stays '0.5.0' and boundary_compat is unchanged ('>=0.5.0 <0.6.0') - a patch bump, not a minor.
